issue.body:
## Description

Makes the Onyx plugin install in Codex CLI as well, from the same directory, and renames that directory from `extensions/claude-code` to `extensions/agent-plugin` since it now serves more than one host. The release tag becomes `agent-plugin/v<version>` and the zip `onyx-agent-plugin.zip`. Nothing has been released from the old path.

- `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` is the Codex manifest. It points hooks at `hooks/codex.json` and declares no MCP server, because a Codex plugin can only bundle a fixed URL and users can't change it. Users add their Onyx server as `onyx` with `codex mcp add`, which the docs already describe.
- `hooks/codex.json` runs the same hook script with a `codex` argument. Codex has no `PostToolUseFailure`, and its hosted web search can't be gated.
- `scripts/hook.ts` now steers without a URL or token (Codex has no options dialog, so only the prefetch needs them), recognises the Onyx tool on a server named `onyx` or `plugin_onyx_onyx`, and continues a Codex turn from `Stop` with a block decision, since Codex replays the reason as the next user prompt.
- `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` at the repo root is the Codex marketplace entry.

Codex ignores bundled hooks in the portable Agent Plugins manifest format, so the manifest uses Codex's own format.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Live in Codex CLI 0.165 with the plugin installed from the repo marketplace and the st-dev MCP server added as `onyx`: a company question made Codex read the skill, call `mcp__onyx__search_indexed_documents` first, answer from an internal doc with its URL, and the `PostToolUse` hook opened the strict gate. With strict retrieval and prefetch on against a stub server, the prefetched sections were cited and the `Stop` nudge came back as a continuation prompt once. `bun test extensions/agent-plugin` covers prompt, prefetch, Stop, replay, a full search clearing the nudge, the Claude Code Stop path, and the strict gate. Hook paths also exercised by hand for both hosts: directive without credentials, strict deny of another server's search tool and of `WebSearch`, allow of the Onyx tool under both server names, allow of non-search tools, gate opening on `PostToolUse`, Stop output in both formats, and the replayed nudge leaving state untouched. The Claude Code side still typechecks with `tsgo` and passes `claude plugin validate` with the same warnings as before.

## Docs

- [x] Customer-facing change: I updated `documentation/` (text and screenshots).
- [ ] No docs change needed (internal, tests, CI, or multi-tenant cloud only).

## Additional Options

- [x] [Optional] Please cherry-pick this PR to the latest release version.

+from onyx.connectors.google_drive.source_operations import (
+    DriveCorpus,
+    GoogleDriveHttpError,
+    GoogleDriveRefreshError,
+    GoogleDriveSourceOperations,
+)
+from onyx.connectors.google_utils.google_utils import GoogleFields
+from onyx.connectors.interfaces import SecondsSinceUnixEpoch
+from onyx.connectors.models import CorpusEstimate, DocumentTypeLabel
+from onyx.file_processing.file_types import OnyxMimeTypes
+from onyx.utils.logger import setup_logger
+from onyx.utils.threadpool_concurrency import (
+    PUSHBACK_OBSERVER,
+    AdaptiveConcurrency,
+    AdaptiveTaskPool,
+    PushbackObserver,
+)
+
+logger = setup_logger()
+
+# Most parts a shard cuts the range ahead into after one page. The page's
+# density sets how many, so a sparse range is not cut into empty parts.
+SHARD_SPLIT_MAX_WAYS = 64
+# Drive keeps modifiedTime to the millisecond. Files inside one second are
+# paged serially rather than cut any finer.
+MIN_SHARD_MS = 1000
+# The end of an open-ended window: a file modified later than this is not
+# expected while the count runs.
+SHARD_END_MARGIN_MS = 3_600_000
+# Seconds between progress reports.
+PROGRESS_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 5.0
+# Ids kept at one modifiedTime stamp to drop a restarted page's repeats.
+# Past this a restart may count a few files at that stamp again.
+MAX_FRONTIER_IDS = 10_000
+# A user without Drive access answers every request with this.
+_NO_DRIVE_ACCESS_STATUS = 401
+# What a shortcut's target is read with: enough to tell whose listing counts it.
+_TARGET_FIELDS = "id, mimeType, size, driveId, owners(emailAddress)"
+
+
+_GOOGLE_APPS_PREFIX = "application/vnd.google-apps."
+_DOCUMENT_MIME_TYPES = {
+    GDriveMimeType.DOC.value,
+    GDriveMimeType.WORD_DOC.value,
+    "application/msword",
+}
+_SPREADSHEET_MIME_TYPES = {
+    GDriveMimeType.SPREADSHEET.value,
+    GDriveMimeType.SPREADSHEET_OPEN_FORMAT.value,
+    GDriveMimeType.SPREADSHEET_MS_EXCEL.value,
+} | OnyxMimeTypes.TABULAR_MIME_TYPES
+_PRESENTATION_MIME_TYPES = {
+    GDriveMimeType.PPT.value,
+    GDriveMimeType.POWERPOINT.value,
+    "application/vnd.ms-powerpoint",
+}
+
+
+def drive_document_type(mime_type: str) -> DocumentTypeLabel:
+    """The shared label a Drive file counts under. A native Google file
+    counts with its Office counterpart. Other Google apps are other files."""
+    if mime_type in _DOCUMENT_MIME_TYPES:
+        return DocumentTypeLabel.DOCUMENT
+    if mime_type in _SPREADSHEET_MIME_TYPES:
+        return DocumentTypeLabel.SPREADSHEET
+    if mime_type in _PRESENTATION_MIME_TYPES:
+        return DocumentTypeLabel.PRESENTATION
+    if mime_type == GDriveMimeType.PDF.value:
+        return DocumentTypeLabel.PDF
+    if mime_type.startswith(_GOOGLE_APPS_PREFIX):
+        return DocumentTypeLabel.OTHER
+    if mime_type in OnyxMimeTypes.TEXT_MIME_TYPES or mime_type.startswith("text/"):
+        return DocumentTypeLabel.TEXT
+    if mime_type.startswith("image/"):
+        return DocumentTypeLabel.IMAGE
+    return DocumentTypeLabel.OTHER
+
+
+def _listed_mime_type(file: GoogleDriveFileType) -> str | None:
+    """The type a listed file counts as: a shortcut counts as its target. A
+    folder shortcut is not a document."""
+    mime_type = file.get("mimeType", "")
+    if mime_type != DRIVE_SHORTCUT_TYPE:
+        return mime_type
+    details = file.get("shortcutDetails") or {}
+    target_type = details.get("targetMimeType")
+    if not isinstance(target_type, str) or target_type == DRIVE_FOLDER_TYPE:
+        return None
+    return target_type
+
+
+def _shortcut_target_id(file: GoogleDriveFileType) -> str | None:
+    if file.get("mimeType") != DRIVE_SHORTCUT_TYPE:
+        return None
+    target_id = (file.get("shortcutDetails") or {}).get("targetId")
+    return target_id if isinstance(target_id, str) else None
+
+
+def _file_size(file: GoogleDriveFileType) -> int | None:
+    """The listed size in bytes, or None when Drive lists the file without one."""
+    try:
+        return int(file["size"])
+    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
+        return None
+
+
+class CountStopped(Exception):
+    """The caller asked the count to stop. Planning the scope raises it too."""
+
+
+# What the estimate says when the count was stopped before the scope was done.
+_STOPPED_NOTE = "stopped before the whole scope was counted"
+
+
+class _Shard(BaseModel):
+    """One listing of a partition over the modifiedTime range [t0, t1), in
+    whole milliseconds so the bounds match Drive's stamps exactly. A work
+    item of this module's threads, not a model other modules read."""
+
+    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
+
+    variant: DriveCorpus
+    user_email: str
+    base_query: str
+    drive_id: str | None
+    # Names the partition in a skip note.
+    what: str
+    t0: int
+    t1: int
+    # Listed by the partition that owns its files, so a file here is counted
+    # without being remembered. Files shared with a user, in a requested
+    # folder, or in a drive only a reader can list are not: they can turn
+    # up on another path, so one a listed drive or My Drive covers is skipped.
+    exact: bool = True
+    # The one listing an OAuth user makes. Its own files are not copies of
+    # what it reaches.
+    oauth: bool = False
+
+    def at(self, t0: int, t1: int) -> "_Shard":
+        return self.model_copy(update={"t0": t0, "t1": t1})
+
+
+def _window_start(start: SecondsSinceUnixEpoch | None) -> int:
+    return math.floor(start * 1000) if start else 0
+
+
+def _window_end(end: SecondsSinceUnixEpoch | None) -> int:
+    """The first millisecond after the window, which the run includes."""
+    if end is not None:
+        return math.floor(end * 1000) + 1
+    return math.ceil(time.time() * 1000) + SHARD_END_MARGIN_MS
+
+
+def _iso(ms: int) -> str:
+    stamp = datetime.fromtimestamp(ms // 1000, tz=timezone.utc)
+    return stamp.replace(microsecond=ms % 1000 * 1000).isoformat(
+        timespec="milliseconds"
+    )
+
+
+def _shard_query(base_query: str, t0: int, t1: int) -> str:
+    field = GoogleFields.MODIFIED_TIME.value
+    return f"{base_query} and {field} >= '{_iso(t0)}' and {field} < '{_iso(t1)}'"
+
+
+def _modified_ms(file: GoogleDriveFileType) -> int:
+    stamp = datetime.fromisoformat(file[GoogleFields.MODIFIED_TIME.value])
+    return round(stamp.timestamp() * 1000)
+
+
+class _CorpusCounter:
+    """Accumulates one estimate from partitions counted on several threads.
+    Every partition goes into one pool: no partition's count depends on
+    another's, so the phases the run walks in order all run at once here."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        ops: GoogleDriveSourceOperations,
+        primary_admin_email: str,
+        is_service_account: bool,
+        scope: DriveCountScope,
+        start: SecondsSinceUnixEpoch | None,
+        end: SecondsSinceUnixEpoch | None,
+        should_stop: Callable[[], bool],
+        on_progress: Callable[[CorpusEstimate], None],
+        concurrency: AdaptiveConcurrency,
+        pool: AdaptiveTaskPool,
+    ) -> None:
+        self._ops = ops
+        self._primary_admin_email = primary_admin_email
+        self._is_service_account = is_service_account
+        self._scope = scope
+        # One window for every partition, so an open end lands on one instant.
+        self._t0 = _window_start(start)
+        self._t1 = _window_end(end)
+        self._should_stop = should_stop
+        self._on_progress = on_progress
+        self._concurrency = concurrency
+        self._pool = pool
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._counts: Counter[DocumentTypeLabel] = Counter()
+        self._bytes: Counter[DocumentTypeLabel] = Counter()
+        # Ids of files that can turn up on several paths, like the run's dedup
+        # set: exact partitions never add to it.
+        self._claimed_file_ids: set[str] = set()
+        # Drives and My Drive owners whose own listing has begun, so a shared
+        # copy of their files is dropped. Until then it is claimed instead.
+        self._listed_drive_ids: set[str] = set()
+        self._listed_owners: set[str] = set()
+        # Set when an OAuth user's one listing begins: which files it reaches.
+        self._oauth_covers: Callable[[GoogleDriveFileType], bool] | None = None
+        # A folder reachable on two paths, or by a shortcut cycle, counts once
+        # per user. Past the cap it may count again.
+        self._visited_folders: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
+        self._last_report = time.monotonic()
+        self.skipped: list[str] = []
+
+    def count_scope(self) -> None:
+        """Runs every partition of the scope on the pool. A stop in any of
+        them stops the whole count."""
+        scope = self._scope
+        tasks: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
+        if not self._is_service_account:
+            # One listing covers the user's files. Drives and folders only
+            # when not every corpus is already in it.
+            if scope.include_my_drives or scope.include_files_shared_with_me:
+                tasks.append(self.count_oauth_files)
+        else:
+            tasks.extend(
+                lambda email=email: self.count_my_drive(email)
+                for email in scope.my_drive_emails
+            )
+        tasks.extend(
+            lambda drive_id=drive_id, email=email: self.count_shared_drive(
+                drive_id, email, complete=drive_id not in scope.incomplete_drive_ids
+            )
+            for drive_id, email in scope.drives.items()
+        )
+        tasks.extend(
+            lambda folder_id=folder_id, email=email: self.count_folder(folder_id, email)
+            for folder_id, emails in scope.folders.items()
+            for email in emails
+        )
+        # Shared listings last: tasks start in order, so most owners are
+        # already listed and few of their files need claiming.
+        if self._is_service_account and scope.include_files_shared_with_me:
+            tasks.extend(
+                lambda email=email: self.count_shared_with_user(email)
+                for email in scope.my_drive_emails
+            )
+        for task in tasks:
+            self._pool.add(task)
+        self._pool.run()
+
+    @property
+    def total(self) -> int:
+        return sum(self._counts.values())
+
+    @property
+    def by_type(self) -> dict[DocumentTypeLabel, int]:
+        return dict(self._counts)
+
+    @property
+    def bytes_by_type(self) -> dict[DocumentTypeLabel, int]:
+        return dict(self._bytes)
+
+    def _skip(self, what: str) -> None:
+        with self._lock:
+            self.skipped.append(what)
+
+    def _check_stop(self) -> None:
+        if self._should_stop():
+            raise CountStopped()
+
+    def _count(self, file: GoogleDriveFileType, shard: _Shard) -> None:
+        self._check_stop()
+        mime_type = _listed_mime_type(file)
+        if mime_type is None:
+            return
+        target_id = _shortcut_target_id(file)
+        sized = file
+        if target_id is None:
+            if not self._admit(file, file.get("id"), shard.exact, shard.oauth):
+                return
+        else:
+            target = self._admit_shortcut_target(file, target_id, shard.user_email)
+            if target is None:
+                return
+            sized = target
+        label = drive_document_type(mime_type)
+        size = _file_size(sized)
+        with self._lock:
+            self._counts[label] += 1
+            if size is not None:
+                self._bytes[label] += size
+            report = self._progress_due()
+        if report is not None:
+            self._on_progress(report)
+
+    def _admit(
+        self,
+        file: GoogleDriveFileType,
+        file_id: object,
+        exact: bool,
+        own_oauth: bool = False,
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Whether the count takes the file: not a copy of one a listing that
+        has begun counts, not one already claimed. One lock, so no listing
+        begins between the coverage check and the claim. Past the dedup cap a
+        duplicate counts again, which over-estimates rather than exhausts
+        memory."""
+        with self._lock:
+            if not exact and self._is_covered(file, own_oauth):
+                return False
+            if not isinstance(file_id, str):
+                return True
+            if file_id in self._claimed_file_ids:
+                return False
+            if not exact and len(self._claimed_file_ids) < MAX_DEDUP_DRIVE_FILE_IDS:
+                self._claimed_file_ids.add(file_id)
+        return True
+
+    def _admit_shortcut_target(
+        self, shortcut: GoogleDriveFileType, target_id: str, user_email: str
+    ) -> GoogleDriveFileType | None:
+        """The target a shortcut counts as, once: None when the target's own
+        listing counts it, when another shortcut already did, or when the
+        user cannot see it, as the run reads it."""
+        details = shortcut.get("shortcutDetails") or {}
+        target = self._ops.get_file(
+            user_email=user_email,
+            file_id=target_id,
+            fields=_TARGET_FIELDS,
+            resource_key=details.get("targetResourceKey"),
+        )
+        if target is None or not self._admit(target, target_id, exact=False):
+            return None
+        return target
+
+    def _progress_due(self) -> CorpusEstimate | None:
+        """A snapshot once per interval. The caller holds the lock."""
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        if now - self._last_report < PROGRESS_INTERVAL_SECONDS:
+            return None
+        self._last_report = now
+        return CorpusEstimate(
+            total_docs=sum(self._counts.values()),
+            docs_by_type=dict(self._counts),
+            bytes_by_type=dict(self._bytes),
+            partial=True,
+            detail=None,
+        )
+
+    def count_shared_drive(self, drive_id: str, email: str, complete: bool) -> None:
+        """Lists the drive as the user the run plans. Only an organizer's
+        listing is a complete record of the drive: another user's can miss
+        limited-access folders, so its files may also arrive on another path."""
+        what = f"shared drive {drive_id}"
+        try:
+            self._count_partition(
+                self._shard(
+                    variant=DriveCorpus.DRIVE,
+                    user_email=email,
+                    base_query=files_in_drive_query(None, None),
+                    drive_id=drive_id,
+                    what=what,
+                    exact=complete,
+                ),
+                started=(
+                    (lambda: self._mark_listed(self._listed_drive_ids, drive_id))
+                    if complete
+                    else None
+                ),
+            )
+        except GoogleDriveHttpError as error:
+            if not error.access_denied:
+                raise
+            self._skip(f"{what} ({email} cannot list it)")
+        except GoogleDriveRefreshError:
+            self._skip(f"{what} (cannot act as {email})")
+
+    def _mark_listed(self, listed: set[str], key: str) -> None:
+        with self._lock:
+            listed.add(key)
+
+    def _shard(
+        self,
+        *,
+        variant: DriveCorpus,
+        user_email: str,
+        base_query: str,
+        what: str,
+        drive_id: str | None = None,
+        exact: bool = True,
+        oauth: bool = False,
+    ) -> _Shard:
+        """A partition's whole window."""
+        return _Shard(
+            variant=variant,
+            user_email=user_email,
+            base_query=base_query,
+            drive_id=drive_id,
+            what=what,
+            t0=self._t0,
+            t1=self._t1,
+            exact=exact,
+            oauth=oauth,
+        )
+
+    def count_my_drive(self, email: str) -> None:
+        what = f"My Drive of {email}"
+        try:
+            self._count_partition(
+                self._shard(
+                    variant=DriveCorpus.USER,
+                    user_email=email,
+                    base_query=my_drive_files_query(False, None, None),
+                    what=what,
+                ),
+                started=lambda: self._mark_listed(self._listed_owners, email.lower()),
+            )
+        except GoogleDriveRefreshError:
+            self._skip(f"{what} (cannot act as the user)")
+        except GoogleDriveHttpError as error:
+            if error.status_code != _NO_DRIVE_ACCESS_STATUS:
+                raise
+            self._skip(f"{what} (no Drive access)")
+
+    def _count_partition(
+        self, shard: _Shard, started: Callable[[], None] | None = None
+    ) -> None:
+        """Counts a whole partition. Its newest file bounds the range first, so
+        the cuts land inside the data instead of in the empty time after it.
+        ``started`` runs once that first request has succeeded."""
+        end = self._newest_ms(shard)
+        if started is not None:
+            started()
+        if end is None:
+            return
+        self._count_sharded(shard.at(shard.t0, min(shard.t1, end + 1)))
+
+    def _newest_ms(self, shard: _Shard) -> int | None:
+        """Drive may answer an empty page with a token, so the listing runs
+        on until a file comes or it ends."""
+        self._check_stop()
+        for item in self._ops.list_files(
+            variant=shard.variant,
+            user_email=shard.user_email,
+            fields=COUNT_FILE_FIELDS,
+            query=_shard_query(shard.base_query, shard.t0, shard.t1),
+            drive_id=shard.drive_id,
+            order_by=f"{GoogleFields.MODIFIED_TIME.value} desc",
+            page_size=1,
+        ):
+            if not isinstance(item, str):
+                return _modified_ms(item)
+        return None
+
+    def _count_sharded(self, shard: _Shard) -> None:
+        """Lists the shard a page at a time in modifiedTime order. After each
+        page the range still ahead is cut into parts: this thread keeps its
+        page token and pages on up to the first cut, the other parts go to the
+        pool as new shards. Nothing is counted twice."""
+        stop_before = shard.t1
+        page_token: str | None = None
+        query = _shard_query(shard.base_query, shard.t0, shard.t1)
+        counted = 0
+        pages = 0
+        # Where the page's files start, for the density the page showed. The
+        # first page starts at its first file, each later one at the last
+        # page's frontier.
+        page_from: int | None = None
+        # Files already passed at the frontier stamp. An expired page token
+        # makes the gateway restart the query, and the listing is ordered, so
+        # a row behind the frontier, or at it and in this set, was seen.
+        frontier_ids: set[str] = set()
+        while True:
+            self._check_stop()
+            more: str | None = None
+            frontier = shard.t0 if page_from is None else page_from
+            listed = 0
+            pages += 1
+            for item in self._ops.list_files(
+                variant=shard.variant,
+                user_email=shard.user_email,
+                fields=COUNT_FILE_FIELDS,
+                query=query,
+                drive_id=shard.drive_id,
+                order_by=GoogleFields.MODIFIED_TIME.value,
+                page_token=page_token,
+                page_size=COUNT_PAGE_SIZE,
+                max_num_pages=1,
+            ):
+                if isinstance(item, str):
+                    more = item
+                    break
+                self._concurrency.observe()
+                modified = _modified_ms(item)
+                if modified >= stop_before:
+                    more = None
+                    break
+                if modified < frontier or (
+                    modified == frontier and item.get("id") in frontier_ids
+                ):
+                    continue
+                if modified > frontier:
+                    frontier_ids.clear()
+                if len(frontier_ids) < MAX_FRONTIER_IDS:
+                    frontier_ids.add(item.get("id", ""))
+                if page_from is None:
+                    page_from = modified
+                listed += 1
+                frontier = modified
+                self._count(item, shard)
+                counted += 1
+            if more is None:
+                logger.debug(
+                    "Shard of %s [%s, %s) done: %s files in %s pages",
+                    shard.what,
+                    _iso(shard.t0),
+                    _iso(stop_before),
+                    counted,
+                    pages,
+                )
+                return
+            page_token = more
+            if page_from is not None:
+                density = listed / max(frontier - page_from, 1)
+                stop_before = self._cut_ahead(shard, frontier, stop_before, density)
+            page_from = frontier
+
+    def _cut_ahead(
+        self, shard: _Shard, frontier: int, stop_before: int, density: float
+    ) -> int:
+        """Hands all but the first part of [frontier, stop_before) to the pool,
+        one part per page the range should hold at ``density`` files per
+        millisecond, and returns where this thread's own part ends."""
+        ahead = stop_before - frontier
+        expected_pages = math.ceil(density * ahead / COUNT_PAGE_SIZE)
+        ways = min(expected_pages, SHARD_SPLIT_MAX_WAYS, ahead // MIN_SHARD_MS)
+        if ways < 2:
+            return stop_before
+        width = ahead // ways
+        cuts = [frontier + width * i for i in range(1, ways)]
+        cuts.append(stop_before)
+        for t0, t1 in zip(cuts, cuts[1:], strict=False):
+            self._pool.add(self._shard_task(shard.at(t0, t1)))
+        logger.debug(
+            "Cut %s ahead of %s into %s parts up to %s",
+            shard.what,
+            _iso(frontier),
+            ways,
+            _iso(stop_before),
+        )
+        return cuts[0]
+
+    def _shard_task(self, shard: _Shard) -> Callable[[], None]:
+        def run() -> None:
+            try:
+                self._count_sharded(shard)
+            except GoogleDriveHttpError as error:
+                if not error.access_denied:
+                    raise
+                self._skip(f"{shard.what} (part of it could not be listed: {error})")
+            except GoogleDriveRefreshError:
+                self._skip(f"{shard.what} (cannot act as the user)")
+
+        return run
+
+    def count_shared_with_user(self, email: str) -> None:
+        """Files the user sees that no listed drive or My Drive covers."""
+        what = f"files shared with {email}"
+        try:
+            self._count_partition(
+                self._shard(
+                    variant=DriveCorpus.USER,
+                    user_email=email,
+                    base_query=my_drive_files_query(True, None, None),
+                    what=what,
+                    exact=False,
+                )
+            )
+        except GoogleDriveRefreshError:
+            self._skip(f"{what} (cannot act as the user)")
+        except GoogleDriveHttpError as error:
+            if error.status_code != _NO_DRIVE_ACCESS_STATUS:
+                raise
+            self._skip(f"{what} (no Drive access)")
+
+    def _is_covered(self, file: GoogleDriveFileType, own_oauth: bool) -> bool:
+        """Whether a listing that has begun counts this file. The OAuth
+        listing's own files are not copies of what it reaches. The caller
+        holds the lock."""
+        return (
+            file.get("driveId") in self._listed_drive_ids
+            or owner_email(file) in self._listed_owners
+            or (
+                not own_oauth
+                and self._oauth_covers is not None
+                and self._oauth_covers(file)
+            )
comment.body: Fixed in 1b67ec6653: the shortcut's target is read with its modifiedTime, and a target modified outside the window skips the coverage check and only goes through the id claim, since no listing of the window reaches it. Covered by test_a_new_shortcut_to_a_file_older_than_the_window_counts_the_target.
Fixed in a82adf005a: folding a source group closes its expanded row, so the runs poll stops. ConnectorListInteractions.test.tsx "closes the expanded row when its source group folds" covers it.

Fixed in e979d0a0db. The fallback state directory moved from the shared temp directory to `~/.cache/onyx-claude-code` (created with mode 0700), so another local user cannot pre-create it or plant links under it. A link inside the user's own home directory is not a boundary the plugin can defend, so there is no ownership check beyond that.

A Stop hook does not need `decision: block` to continue the turn. The Claude Code hooks reference lists `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` as a Stop output: "Non-error feedback for Claude. The conversation continues so Claude can act on it, but unlike decision: block it is shown in the transcript as hook feedback rather than a hook error." ## Description

Adds the Onyx plugin for Claude Code under `extensions/claude-code`, so Onyx is consulted before any other MCP server or plugin.

- A `UserPromptSubmit` hook injects one directive with every question prompt: call `search_indexed_documents` before answering from company knowledge and before any other search tool. No network call, so prompts are never delayed and nothing installed alongside can outrank it. Claude decides when a question needs Onyx and runs the full search pipeline only then.
- The Onyx MCP server is bundled with `alwaysLoad` and the user's token from the plugin's `userConfig` dialog, and now sends connect-time `instructions` so every client calls `search_indexed_documents` first.
- Optional strict retrieval: a `PreToolUse` hook denies other servers' search tools and `WebSearch` until the Onyx tool has run for the prompt.
- Optional prefetch, off by default: the hook posts the prompt to `POST /api/search/raw` from #17261 with a 3 second budget and injects the top sections with rules for when the full tool is still worth a call. A failed or 404 search injects the plain directive. With strict retrieval, a turn that ends on prefetched sections alone gets one `Stop` nudge to run the full search.
- Published as a release zip: a tag-triggered workflow builds `extensions/claude-code` into a GitHub release asset that the hosted `marketplace.json` points at, so users never clone the repo.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Live: installed the plugin from a local marketplace into Claude Code, configured it against st-dev with a PAT, and a headless `claude -p` session with a company question called `mcp__plugin_onyx_onyx__search_indexed_documents` first, before any other tool, and cited Onyx docs. ## Description

Adds the Onyx plugin for Claude Code under `extensions/claude-code`, so Onyx is consulted before any other MCP server or plugin.

- A `UserPromptSubmit` hook injects one directive with every question prompt: call `search_indexed_documents` before answering from company knowledge and before any other search tool. issue.title: MCP search takes too long per call and always times out
issue.body:
## Title
MCP search takes 30–100 seconds per call and times out in my client; need a way to skip the LLM re-check step

**In plain terms:** the MCP search tool is too slow to use. A single search takes 30 to 100 seconds, because Onyx asks the language model to re-check the results before returning them, and there is no way to turn that off. My MCP client gives up after 60 seconds, so many searches never reach me even though Onyx finishes them and returns "success". Finding the documents takes under a second. The extra AI re-checking step is what makes it slow. I'd like a way to skip that step so MCP search returns quickly.

## Environment
- Onyx: `4.9.2` (Docker Compose, stock `docker-compose.yml`, `latest` images)
- Docker Desktop on Windows with WSL2, about 15 GB of memory available to containers
- 14 containers, all healthy, about 15 h uptime, 0 restarts, no OOM kills
- Embeddings: local `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1` on CPU, 0.04–0.6 s per embed call
- LLM: `ollama_chat` via litellm. First Ollama cloud (`mistral-large-3:675b`), then a local Ollama with a small 4B-class model (16k and 32k context variants)
- MCP client with a 60 s per-call limit, calling `POST /mcp/`
- Data: PDFs through the File connector, including one very large PDF (about 1,450 pages)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Index a large PDF with the File connector.
2. Call the MCP tool `search_indexed_documents` with an ordinary query (also try `skip_query_expansion: true`).
3. Watch `api_server` logs and the nginx access log.

## Expected
A retrieval-only path, or a documented way to skip or limit LLM document selection, so MCP calls return in seconds.

## Actual
The tool description says each call runs "the full Onyx search pipeline (LLM query expansion, hybrid retrieval, document selection, context expansion)". `skip_query_expansion=true` did not avoid the LLM calls. In the `api_server` logs, each `/search` does: embed query (fast), retrieve (fast), then one document-selection LLM call, then about 3–10 `classify_section_relevance` calls, then `run took N seconds`.

- nginx `POST /mcp/` response times (s): 38.5, 34.2, 30.2, 64.2, 33.8, 44.4, 72.6, 103.6, 80.8, 83.9
- Response sizes: 408–599 KB each
- `run took` (cloud model): 44.3, 72.5, 103.6, 80.7, 83.8 s
- `run took` (local 4B-class model, 100% GPU): 53.6 and 76.9 s
- Calls above 60 s were abandoned by the client, but Onyx still returned HTTP 200
- With default Ollama parallelism the `classify_section_relevance` completions were evenly spaced (about 13 s apart), consistent with serial handling. With `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=4` they arrived in two bunches, but the whole run still took 76.9 s
- Two requests logged `document_filter.py:404 Error calling LLM for document selection: LLM streaming call exceeded its total timeout`
- The rest of the stack was healthy during all of this (OpenSearch 4.5 GB, near-idle CPU, `/api/health` 17–64 ms)
- The same timeouts happen with small documents: searching for ordinary 2–4 page PDFs also failed. When a client sends several searches at once, they queue behind each other (the LLM steps are handled serially), so every call exceeds the client's 60 s limit.

## What I looked for
I checked `env.template` and `docker-compose.yml` and found no `DISABLE_LLM_*` or relevance/selection option. Only commented-out `LLM_SOCKET_READ_TIMEOUT`, `CONTEXTUAL_RAG_LLM_TIMEOUT` and `MAX_DOCUMENT_CHARS` look related. I did not search the docs or source, so a setting may exist that I missed.

## Requested change
1. An MCP search option (or env var) to skip or cap LLM document selection and return retrieval results only.
2. Document the latency and the LLM dependency in the MCP tool description or docs.
3. Consider smaller MCP responses (see below).

## Related notes
**Large, apparently duplicated response text.** Each returned chunk's text appeared twice, with straight vs curly quotes, in responses of 408–599 KB. I suspect the PDF has both an embedded text layer and an OCR layer, but this is **unverified**. It could be two layers indexed, or a result-formatting problem. Related to my earlier indexing report: `https://github.com/onyx-dot-app/onyx/issues/16461`.

**Log noise on a plain Docker Compose install** (I did not check for existing issues):
- `background`: `cleanup_idle_sandboxes` raises a Kubernetes `ConfigException: Invalid kube-config file. No configuration found.` with a full traceback every minute
- `background`: `monitor_process_memory` logs `Duplicate process type for type beat ...` and `Missing processes: {...}` every minute
- `api_server`: on every LLM-related request, `model_capabilities.py:391 Cannot find reasoning for name=mistral-large-3:675b and provider=ollama_chat` (ERROR) plus about 20 `No catalog entry found for ollama_chat/<model>` warnings

Part of [ENG-4403](https://linear.app/onyx-app/issue/ENG-4403)

The connector page's status strip becomes the spec's status cards.

- Cards: two cards on LineLayout 8 px apart, Indexing first, then Permissions Sync for permission-synced sources. Column A holds the label and the tag line: a size-24 Tag, then the stage hint while a run is live or the prune and checks hints when idle. A paused pair shows no hints.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This PR supersedes #17035. Merge this PR and close #17035 without merging.

## Description

Refs #16500 (first request). Mirror of #17035 by @oedokumaci. After review, no-LLM search is its own route, `POST /search/raw`, instead of a flag on `POST /search`, and its results keep their surrounding chunks.

`POST /search` makes several LLM or decision-model calls per search: query expansion, source and time detection, federated Slack query building, document selection and per-section relevance checks. A caller that ranks results itself, such as an MCP client or the Claude Code plugin hook, waits and pays for calls it does not need.

- `POST /search/raw` takes the `/search` filters (`query`, `sources`, `document_sets`, `tags`, `time_cutoff`, `persona_id`) plus `context_chunks` (0 to 5, default 5). It runs retrieval on the query as written and returns up to 10 sections (`MAX_SELECTED_SECTIONS`) in retrieval order, each with up to `context_chunks` neighbors on each side. Send 0 for the matched passages only.
- It needs `read:search`, like `/search`. It runs the API-key usage check but no LLM cost, model spend or token budget check, since it spends no tokens. It is on the MCP OAuth route allowlist.
- The MCP `search_indexed_documents` tool's `retrieval_only`, and `MCP_SERVER_SEARCH_RETRIEVAL_ONLY=true`, call `/search/raw`.
- `/search` and `/search/raw` share persona loading, filters, tool lookup, and the trace and response mapping in `api.py`. `search_utils.expand_section_with_neighbors` is the one neighbor-expansion path, also used by the full-document branch of `expand_section_with_context`.

`/search/raw` still builds the default LLM object because `SearchTool` needs one, so the deployment needs an LLM provider. It never calls it. Chat search does not change.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- Live: I ran this branch's API against a copy of a dev database and its OpenSearch index, while the route was still at `/retrieve`. It returned 10 results in 0.7 s with `context_chunks: 0`, about 2k characters each. The route contract manifest includes `/search/raw`.
- Integration: `test_basic_search_returns_results` runs against both routes. I did not run the integration suite locally.

issue.title: feat(google-drive): count the corpus beside the fetch, sharded by modified time

labels.name: repo-3fb41926
labels.description: Skip CodeRabbit review on this PR

issue.body:
## Description

Stacked on https://github.com/onyx-dot-app/onyx/pull/16747.

Why: Google Drive is the first source to report corpus size and count time to the fleet.

Fix:
- `google_drive/corpus_estimate.py` implements `CorpusEstimateConnector` with a metadata-only `files.list` over the same partitions the run walks (shared drives, My Drives, files shared with each user, requested folders), 1,000 files per page, all in one `AdaptiveTaskPool`.
- The connector resolves what to count (`DriveCountScope`) with the run's own methods: the user per shared drive, the users, and the principals per requested folder. A drive nobody can list or a folder nobody can see is reported, and a drive only a reader can list is a lower bound.
- Time sharding: each partition reads its newest file first, lists in `modifiedTime` order one page at a time, and after each page cuts the range ahead into as many shards as that page's density says it holds. A big drive fans out across the pool within a few pages.
- A file that can turn up on several paths (shared with a user, in a requested folder, behind a shortcut, in a reader-listed drive) counts once: it is dropped when the listing that owns it has begun and claimed by id otherwise, up to the run's dedup cap.
- The rate limits and server errors `google_utils.py` waits out are recorded as pushback, so the pool's limit settles where Drive stops pushing back.

Measured on a 1,031,726-document workspace: 5 min 21 s, down from 47 min listed serially. Drive's per-drive listing rate is the ceiling, not our thread count.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Unit tests against a fake gateway (`test_drive_corpus_estimate.py`): labels per mime type, counts by type and bytes, each drive listed as its planned user, a reader-listed drive as a lower bound, a shared file counted once, a shortcut counted as its target once with the target's bytes, a folder inside a listed My Drive counted once, an OAuth listing overlapping listed drives counted once, a user without Drive access skipped, a user who cannot be impersonated losing nothing, what nobody can list reported, a stop checked between requests, an empty first page with a token, a restarted page, the inclusive window end, big partitions split by modified time, folders and subfolders, files inside one second. Live on dev1: pair 2808 on the onyx.app workspace counted 1,031,726 documents in 6 min 25 s beside the fetch, with the same total as a serial listing. The fleet event itself has not been seen server side, since the fleet service does not accept the `corpus` type yet.
